verdict.line: You lose if you eat Boomerang Throw poke for free before level 6; you win once Demacian Justice is up and you can force all-ins he can't kite.

brief.thesis: Gnar is a ranged poke champion with no answer to prolonged melee pressure once you're on top of him, while Garen has no way to close distance except the move speed burst on Q (Decisive Strike). The whole lane is about whether Gnar's Boulder Toss (16-10s cooldown, 1100 range) chips you down before you get an all-in window, which is exactly why the numbers sit at a near-even 50.5% over 2163 games despite Gnar holding the early lane and solo-kill edge.

theirWindow.when: Mini Gnar, Boomerang Throw off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He throws the boomerang at up to 1100 range to damage and slow you, then auto-attacks with Hyper active for bonus damage and move speed while staying outside your 300-325 range. Don't stand in minion-clear range when his Q is up.

yourWindow.when: His Q is on cooldown and you're in melee
yourWindow.what: Pop Q (Decisive Strike) to break any slow and silence him on your next hit, then chain E (Judgment) while he can't disengage — he has no gap-closer back except Hop, which only travels further off a unit's head.

start.why: 51% win rate over 2104 games and 80.2% pick rate — the flat damage reduction on being hit directly offsets Boomerang Throw chip damage.

boots.why: 52.2% win rate over 1560 games and the most-picked boots — the attack speed keeps Judgment's uptime and auto-weaves high once you're in melee range.

core.why: Gives you a gap-closer and slow of your own so Gnar can't just kite you with Boulder Toss.
Attack speed and move speed to keep pace with Hop/Crunch resets.
Part of the 56.1% win rate core path over 328 games; grievous wounds matters once fights go long.

you're ahead and want faster cooldowns to chain duels after a kill

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks in extended melee trades and heals you back, which is the only way to outlast Gnar's poke once you've closed the gap.

summoners.why: 87.8% pick rate and the best win rate of the three options (51.3%) — Ignite punishes the all-in window once Demacian Justice comes online at 6.

playing.title: Don't trade without Q up
playing.detail: Decisive Strike's move speed burst is your only way to close distance and land a clean hit; wasting it on cooldown leaves you stuck eating Boomerang Throw for free.

playing.title: Bait the boomerang onto minions
playing.detail: Boulder Toss has a 16-10s cooldown — if he throws it into the wave instead of you, that's your window to walk up and punish before it's back.

playing.title: Track the Rage bar for Mega transform
playing.detail: Mega Gnar trades Hyper's ranged poke for Wallop, a stun smash in front of him — don't walk into melee range right as he transforms.

playing.title: Hold all-ins for level 6
playing.detail: Demacian Justice threatens an execute Gnar can't out-trade; this is your clearest window to flip lane control per the measured data.

playing.title: Let Perseverance heal between pokes
playing.detail: Garen's passive regenerates a percentage of max health per second out of combat — back off after a poke exchange instead of forcing a second trade.

playing.title: Respect Hop's range when low
playing.detail: Hop lets him bounce off your head for extra distance at 475 range; don't overextend at low HP expecting him to be stuck.

playing.title: Watch for GNAR! at 16+
playing.detail: Once Mega Gnar's ultimate is up (cooldown drops to 0s at rank 3), a knockback into a wall stuns and adds bonus damage — don't fight with your back to terrain.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners and the 50.5% head-to-head win rate over 2163 games are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch; the lane-by-lane tactical reading is my own analysis of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit by Mini Gnar’s third (W) by keeping your distance. Close in to engage him whenever your skills come off cooldown. Try to kill him after reaching level 6 to gain lane control.
